newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv military headquarters named after Rabin.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv military headquarters named after Rabin.

text.p: Israel renamed its military headquarters in Tel Aviv after late prime minister Yitzhak Rabin on Monday, the first anniversary of the soldier-turned- peacemaker's assassination.

"Of all the places I have been, there is no place harder for me and stranger for me and sadder for me to be than here in his place -- because this was his home for so many years," his widow Leah told a sombre ceremony.

Rabin, whose 27-year army career began before Israel's founding in 1948, led the Jewish state to victory as army chief during the 1967 Middle East War. He served for years as defence minister and prime minister.
"Beyond his family and his private house, this was his home and this was his family," Leah Rabin told a crowd that included generals past and present.
Yigal Amir, a Jewish gunman opposed to Rabin's moves to settle the Arab-Israeli conflict, killed the 73-year-old leader after a Tel Aviv peace rally on November 4, 1995.
"The General Staff Camp today becomes Yitzhak Rabin Camp," said Lieutenant-General Amnon Shahak, the army chief.

"Yitzhak Rabin laboured for years here in the nerve centre of the army and his heart in those years and in all other years was there with the soldiers -- a true soldier in the beautiful meaning of the word, in the moral meaning, a bold, wise, skilled, clever soldier -- attentive to his people, Mr Security."
